What comes up in Merewether

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. Treat the rows as the usual shape of the job locally. A specific property can differ, and that is what a site visit settles.

Tight coastal block with no side access

The characteristic Merewether constraint, and the thing that sets the programme.

How it is handled
Smaller plant or hand demolition with material carried out and loaded at the kerb in sequenced loads.
What does it
Mini excavator, hand tools, tippers staged at the street.

Weathered sheeting on an older dwelling

Eaves, roofing and wall sheeting that decades of salt air have broken down.

How it is handled
Condition assessed before disturbance, removed under the appropriate controls, then independent clearance before demolition starts.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, with air monitoring where the condition requires it.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Merewether

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Older coastal housing on tight blocks Almost all of it pre 1990, with neighbours close on both sides.
  • Heavy coastal exposure Which breaks cement sheet down and can move it from bonded to friable.
  • Limited side access Pushing work towards smaller plant and material carried out.
  • High land value and steady redevelopment Knockdown rebuilds on blocks that were originally modest.

Merewether blocks are tight and the streets are narrow, so the side gap decides the machine and the kerb decides the vehicle. Both are settled at the site visit, because getting either wrong turns a fixed price into a variation.

Merewether questions

What people ask before we start

Does the salt air really change how asbestos is handled?
Yes. Weathered cement sheet can have to be handled as friable rather than bonded, which means a higher licence class, full enclosure, air monitoring and a different clearance process. The condition is assessed on site before anything is touched.
There is no side access. What are the options?
Smaller plant, hand demolition where it is needed, and material carried out to the kerb. It is slower than an open site and it is priced that way rather than discovered later.
Do you work around the lake as well as in Newcastle itself?
Yes. Charlestown, Warners Bay, Belmont and the surrounding suburbs are part of the same coverage, along with Maitland inland.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
